<cite ref="Bava Kamma 46b">B. Kam. 46ᵇ</cite>, v. <cite ref="K00005"><he>כְּאֵב</he> I</cite>.
Lam. R. to II, 1 אית … לכ׳ עייבא there is a place where they call a sore ͑ayba (heaviness), v. כְּאֵב I Pa.—Esp. ulcer, ulceration (mostly as a collective noun).

<cite ref="Shabbat 62b:20">Sabb. 62ᵇ</cite> (ref. to <cite ref="Isaiah 3:24">Is. III, 24</cite>) <he>חלף שופרי כ׳</he> instead of beauty ulcers; [Kimḥi quotes <cite ref="K00175"><he>כְּוָאָה</he></cite>; Ms. M. <he>כיבא כיאורא</he>, combining two versions].
<cite ref="Kiddushin 81a">Ib. 81ᵃ</cite> [read:] <he>יתיב עליה מלא נפשיה שיחנא וכ׳</he> he sat down before it (the tray), his body being full of &c.—

<cite ref="Shabbat 67a:6">Sabb. 67ᵃ</cite> <he>לכ׳ לימא הכי</he> Ar. (ed. <cite ref="K00614"><he>כיפא</he></cite>, Ar. s. v. <cite ref="K00886"><he>כס</he></cite> :<he>כיסא</he>) against ulcers say the following charm.—Pl. <he>כֵּיבִין</he>.

<cite ref="Shabbat 67a:6">Ib.</cite> <he>שיחנין וכ׳</he> Ms. M. (ed. <he>שחינ׳ כְּאֵיבִין</he>, read <he>ש׳ וכ׳</he>).—[<cite ref="Kohelet Rabbah 1:2">Koh. R. to I, 2</cite>, v. <cite ref="B00541"><he>בִּיב</he></cite>.]
